name: Neofeminism
summary: Neofeminism is a contemporary and popular-culture feminism holding that women are empowered by embracing femininity, appearance, lifestyle and sexuality as personal choices. It keeps legal equality, takes an intersectional line, criticises rigid gender norms for men as well as women, and sees equality as positive-sum. Scholarly accounts (Radner) trace it to Helen Gurley Brown and note its consumerist, neoliberal-compatible character.
scope: Represents the choice-and-femininity strand described in Wikipedia and in Hilary Radner's Neo-Feminist Cinema, with Helen Gurley Brown's Sex and the Single Girl (1962) as its forerunner. It excludes Zephir's 1980s French sense (essentialist ecriture feminine) and the older sense of any new feminist activism. The sources describe a cultural outlook, not a programme, so most economic and institutional answers are inferences and low confidence.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Neofeminism's sources never discuss health policy; a liberal, gender-equality outlook plus concern for women's care access suggests mild support.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Radner's neofeminism stresses work as a necessity for women; better pay for low-paid working women follows loosely, though no source states it.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Radner ties neofeminism to neoliberal values, but the choice-feminist strand is silent on markets versus state, so adherents plausibly split.

public-ownership.rationale: Neofeminism as described is consumer-culture friendly and has no nationalisation programme, so adherents would lean against it by inference.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The sources give no tax position; a gender-equality outlook leans left while the career-and-consumer ethos leans the other way.

unions-good.rationale: Brown's single-girl ethic stresses individual advancement through work rather than collective bargaining; sources do not address unions.

property-fundamental.rationale: No source addresses property rights; individual autonomy points one way and egalitarianism the other.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Not discussed; Radner portrays neofeminism as comfortable with consumer capitalism while critics note its limits.

cut-welfare.rationale: Gender-equality advocacy normally supports social protection for women, so adherents likely reject cutting welfare, though no source states this.

worker-ownership.rationale: Nothing in neofeminism's sources advocates collective ownership; its focus is individual women's careers and choices.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Autonomy and personal-choice emphasis suggests wariness of surveillance, but this is inferred, not documented.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Neofeminist sources never address drug policy; adherents likely split.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Intersectional concern for harm to marginalised groups pulls toward restriction while pop-culture individualism pulls toward free expression; undocumented.

strong-leader.rationale: Neofeminism critiques hierarchy in gender norms and has no strongman tradition; inferred rejection.

state-harmful.rationale: Neofeminism retains legal equality and works within existing institutions, so rejecting the idea the state is wholly harmful is a safe inference.

limit-guns.rationale: Mainstream pop-feminist and liberal views lean toward gun limits; no source states it, so inferred.

empower-police-military.rationale: Not discussed; liberal-feminist outlook leans against expanding police and military power.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Neofeminism celebrates sexual agency and personal choice, so adherents plausibly back consenting adult sex work, though sources do not name it.

rehabilitation.rationale: Liberal-progressive default and intersectional awareness suggest rehabilitation; undocumented.

traditional-family.rationale: Brown celebrated single women and sex outside marriage, and neofeminism challenges restrictive gender norms, so it does not treat the traditional family as foundational.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Neofeminism takes an intersectional approach and challenges restrictive gender norms, so support is the documented-leaning view though marriage equality is not named.

abortion-legal.rationale: Pro-choice stance follows from its emphasis on women's autonomy over their bodies and sexuality; the sources do not name abortion itself.

more-religion-public.rationale: Not addressed; secular, sexually liberal outlook suggests adherents would not want more public religion.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Its intersectional approach implies support for addressing racial injustice, though policies are not specified.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The Wikipedia article says neofeminism critiques the social construction of the gender binary, but it also celebrates femininity, so agreement is moderate.

gradual-change.rationale: Neofeminism keeps legal equality and works through culture and personal life rather than revolution, but sources do not state a view on pace.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Intersectional, liberal orientation suggests opposition; no source addresses immigration.

free-trade.rationale: Radner links neofeminism with neoliberalism but sources do not name trade; split.

nation-first.rationale: Inferred from its liberal, intersectional and consumer-global outlook.

open-borders.rationale: Not addressed; intersectionality leans open, mainstream pop feminism leans moderate.

limit-growth.rationale: Radner's neofeminism is bound up with consumer culture and growth, so limiting growth is unlikely to be endorsed; inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Mainstream progressive default; none of the sources discuss climate.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: No neofeminist source takes a view on technological optimism, so adherents are treated as split.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nuclear power is outside neofeminism's concerns, and no source gives a position on it.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Conflicts with personal-choice and expression emphasis.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Islamic jurisprudence on jihad is outside neofeminism.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Takfiri rebellion is foreign to neofeminism.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Participatory democracy is not discussed in neofeminist sources.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The Wikipedia article says neofeminism takes an intersectional approach, but it is not its central doctrine.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Challenging the gender binary and an intersectional approach point to support, though not explicitly documented.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Neofeminist sources do not comment on the left-right divide.

alienated-labor.rationale: Radner presents work as a necessity and source of independence rather than alienation.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Divine right of authority conflicts with its secular, personal-choice outlook.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed; secularism and personal choice about appearance pull opposite ways.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Gender-equality advocacy implies support, though not discussed in sources.

social-market-economy.rationale: Radner ties neofeminism to neoliberal values, but the social-market model is not discussed.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Disarmament is not discussed; reformist outlook leans against abolition.

rich-first.rationale: Unbalanced development doctrine is not discussed.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutualist credit is not part of neofeminism, which accepts consumer-credit economy.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Not addressed; ecofeminist claim, not part of neofeminist sources.

reification.rationale: Marxist theory of commodity fetishism is not part of neofeminism, though critics of Radner's consumer-culture account touch on it.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Media ownership critique is not part of neofeminism, which works through commercial pop culture.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Rule-of-law doctrine is not discussed specifically.

online-participation.rationale: E-democracy is not covered by neofeminist sources.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Religious reform is not addressed in the sources.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Wealth concentration is not discussed; Radner's neoliberal link pulls opposite to the equality premise.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Abolitionism is not part of neofeminism; reformist outlook leans against.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The sources do not weigh charity against welfare; equality concerns lean against.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is not part of neofeminism.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Existential risk is not discussed in the sources.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Gender equality is central to neofeminism, and Brown rejected the idea that single women must be subordinate to husbands.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Resident voting rights are not addressed.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Drilled youth movements conflict with personal-choice emphasis and are foreign to neofeminism.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Nuclear basing policy is not discussed.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Recognition politics is not covered by neofeminist sources.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Radner's neofeminism stresses women's income from work.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Absolute pacifism is not part of neofeminism.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Primordial nationalism is not part of neofeminism; inferred rejection.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Neofeminism critiques the social construction of the gender binary but celebrates femininity; sex itself is not discussed.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed; celebrating femininity pulls against, intersectionality toward.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Nationalist martyr cults are not part of neofeminism.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Cosmic good-versus-evil politics is foreign to neofeminism.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Spiritual Zionism-style views are not covered.

god-not-male.rationale: Feminist theology is not addressed in neofeminist sources.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Feminist scriptural criticism is not part of neofeminism's sources.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Territorial unification demands are not discussed.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: A socialist definitional debate foreign to neofeminism.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Municipal services ownership is not addressed.

municipal-property.rationale: Municipalist ownership is not part of neofeminism.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Libertarian municipalism is not part of neofeminism.

family-wage.rationale: Neofeminism, per Radner and Brown, assumes women earn their own wages; a male-breadwinner family wage conflicts.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Drug regulation speed is not discussed.

online-anonymity.rationale: Pseudonymity online is not addressed in the sources.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Spirituality in politics is not part of neofeminism.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed; Brown's urban career ethos mild support but undocumented.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Not addressed; intersectionality favors recognising groups but not racial organising per se.

racial-pride.rationale: Racial pride is not discussed; adherents plausibly split.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Linguistic nationalism is not part of neofeminism.

communal-electorates.rationale: Separate electorates are not discussed; inferred mild rejection from a universal-equality premise.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Neofeminism celebrates femininity but also holds that gender norms are socially constructed, so adherents split on women's distinct public values.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Monopoly of force is not discussed.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Conscientious refusal is not addressed; mild rejection inferred.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Wage-setting structure is not discussed in neofeminism.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Global economic order reform is not discussed.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Smashing the state conflicts with a movement based on legal equality.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Panarchist economic pluralism is not discussed.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Natural capital accounting is not covered.

sacred-nation.rationale: Sacralised nationalism is not part of neofeminism.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Student debt is not addressed in the sources.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Internal colonial theory is not part of neofeminism.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Not addressed; critique of gender construction pulls away.

public-service-media.rationale: Public broadcasting is not discussed; adherents likely indifferent.

workers-own-party.rationale: A labour-party doctrine is not part of neofeminism.

ban-fgm.rationale: Bodily autonomy and gender equality; undocumented.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Equal legal rights is central to its commitment to legal gender equality.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Linguistic classification disputes are not addressed.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Libertarian environmental liability is not covered.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Customary authority is not discussed; mild rejection inferred from its liberal outlook.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Sentencing policy is not covered; liberal default leans against.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Language requirements for immigrants are not discussed.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Not addressed; a Marxist-Leninist question outside neofeminism.

premarital-sex.rationale: Brown's Sex and the Single Girl encouraged sexual relationships before or without marriage and defended single women's sexuality.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: The sources are about culture and lifestyle and never mention unions; adherents with neoliberal-compatible and left-leaning views would split.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred from its intersectional, equality-minded outlook, which tends to see ID rules as a barrier to some voters; no source addresses it.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from its liberal, intersectional pluralism; the sources do not discuss church-state questions.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Neofeminism has no theory of democracy; a liberal outlook favours elections but adherents also expect policy substance.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from a liberal, choice-and-expression outlook that would oppose cutting access; no source addresses it.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Radner ties neofeminism to neoliberal values, but its sources never discuss welfare design; adherents would split.

women-suffrage.rationale: Neofeminism keeps legal equality for women, as described in the Wikipedia account, so equal voting and office-holding rights are a given.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Its sources focus on femininity and consumer culture rather than religion; a choice-based outlook would not treat religion as a major cause of oppression.

race-social-construct.rationale: Its intersectional line, as described on Wikipedia, accepts the mainstream view that race is socially constructed.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: It keeps legal equality and an intersectional line, which fits support for equality bodies, though the sources describe culture rather than institutions.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred: the sources describe a cultural outlook and say nothing of how property is first acquired.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from its liberal, intersectional and positive-sum view of equality, which supports accountability for atrocities.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred: a choice-centred, lifestyle feminism fits poorly with literal scriptural authority.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from its intersectional line and commitment to women's equality, which would want it written into self-rule.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred: a consumerist, neoliberal-compatible outlook is unlikely to defend a planned state.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred: the sources describe a cultural outlook and say nothing on how offices are filled.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred from its legal-equality and choice emphasis, which cuts against giving one church legal privilege.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred: the sources are silent on ethnic territorial autonomy.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred: the sources are silent on territorial disputes.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred: the sources are silent on colonial borders.

simple-living.rationale: Radner describes it as consumerist, valuing fashion, appearance and lifestyle, which cuts against limiting needs.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred: the sources are silent on settlement in Indigenous homelands.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from its legal equality and its criticism of rigid gender norms for men as well as women.

missingStatements.text: Women should be free to use their appearance, femininity and sexuality as sources of personal empowerment.
missingStatements.rationale: The central claim of neofeminism is that femininity and sexuality embraced as personal choice are empowering.
missingStatements.declined: Too vague to be contested; covered loosely by legalize-sex-work and gender-identity questions.

missingStatements.text: Financial independence through paid work is essential to women's freedom.
missingStatements.rationale: Radner's neofeminism, following Brown, treats work as a necessity for women and the basis of their independence.
missingStatements.declined: Not contested enough across ideologies to justify a bank slot; paid-care-work and job-guarantee cover work and independence.

missingStatements.text: Sex before or outside marriage is acceptable for women.
missingStatements.rationale: Brown's Sex and the Single Girl encouraged sexual relationships before or without marriage and defended single women's sexuality.

notes: Neofeminism is thinly documented as a political programme; Radner portrays it as neoliberal and consumerist, while Wikipedia stresses intersectionality and positive-sum equality. Critics such as Betty Friedan called Brown's message anti-feminist.
